summary: A zero-sugar nootropic energy drink in a can from UK brand Neutonic. Each 330ml can gives 120mg natural caffeine, 500mg citicoline (as Cognizin®), 400mg L-theanine, 400mg rhodiola extract and 200mg Panax ginseng extract, plus eight B vitamins. Caffeine, citicoline and L-theanine meet our reference doses; the rhodiola extract states no standardisation, and we have no reference dose on file for ginseng. With Japan selected, neutonic.com sells it from its main store in pounds sterling (GBP), and we found no Japan-specific shipping terms on its pages (checked 2026-10-19); its product page says 'Worldwide shipping available'.
whatItIs: Neutonic Productivity Drink is a carbonated, ready-to-drink can from Neutonic, a UK brand whose range also includes caffeine-free Brain Capsules. One can is one serving ('Each can contains one serving'), and the vendor's recommended serving is one can a day. With Japan selected, neutonic.com sells it in packs of 12 cans in one flavour (White Peach, Tropical Ice, Strawberry Lemonade, Wild Citrus, Blue Raspberry or Orange Sunrise) or as a mixed-flavour pack. Besides the actives, the ingredient list names carbonated water, the acidity regulators citric acid and trisodium citrate, natural flavourings, the sweeteners sucralose and acesulfame K, and potassium sorbate as a preservative; the vitamin blend lists niacin, pantothenic acid, vitamin B6, riboflavin, thiamine, folic acid (as L-methylfolate), biotin and vitamin B12 (as methylcobalamin), which the vendor's panel gives as 100% of the reference intake (RI). The vendor says the drink is suitable for vegetarians and vegans.
howItWorks: Caffeine (120mg) blocks adenosine receptors; at low-to-moderate doses it consistently improves alertness, vigilance, attention and reaction time, with less consistent effects on memory (McLellan 2016, a narrative review). L-theanine (400mg, twice the top of our 100-200mg reference range) is an amino acid from green tea: in an 11-study meta-analysis, caffeine plus L-theanine had moderate effects versus placebo on alertness and attention-switching accuracy (Camfield 2014), but Foxe 2012 found no added benefit over either compound alone, and in a controlled trial (Rogers 2008, PubMed 17891480) L-theanine did not significantly reduce caffeine jitteriness. Citicoline (500mg, as Cognizin®) is a precursor to acetylcholine and phosphatidylcholine; its memory evidence comes from older adults with inefficient memory at 1,000-2,000mg a day (Spiers 1996), and a Cochrane review found no evidence of an attention benefit in older adults with chronic cerebral disorders. Rhodiola is an adaptogen: small trials of the SHR-5 extract found less mental fatigue, but a 2012 systematic review rated every included study at high or unclear risk of bias, and the product page does not say which extract or standardisation is used. We have no reference dose on file for Panax ginseng. Neutonic Productivity Drink itself has not been tested in a published trial; the vendor's claims rest on ingredient-level research.
whatToExpect: Caffeine's alerting effect typically starts within 15-45 minutes, the onset on our caffeine page; the vendor suggests a can before 'any high demand session', from a morning start to training. Each can has 120mg caffeine and the vendor recommends one can a day, advising drinkers to be mindful of their total caffeine intake, so count it toward your daily total if you also drink coffee. Citicoline's memory effects in trials were measured after 2-3 months, so a single can should not be expected to change memory. With Japan selected, neutonic.com offers 12-can packs one-time or on a subscription (Subscribe & Save 15%), priced in pounds sterling (checked 2026-10-19). The product page says 'Worldwide shipping available'; we found no Japan-specific shipping terms on neutonic.com, and its shipping help article says 'If you're ordering from outside one of our local fulfilment regions, your order may be subject to import duties, taxes, VAT or customs processing fees.' (checked 2026-10-19).

whatItIs: Neutonic Brain Capsules (UK edition) are the caffeine-free capsules Neutonic sells on its main store, which serves Japan in pounds sterling. They carry the UK label rather than the US one: the actives and amounts are the same as on the US bottle, but this label prints no bacoside standardisation for the bacopa extract (the US label states 55% bacosides), its ingredient list names 'Panax Ginseng Root' where its dose panel says '200mg Panax Ginseng Extract', and the capsule shell is rice hull concentrate and hypromellose coloured with iron oxide and titanium dioxide. A bottle holds 90 capsules, 30 daily servings of 3; the vendor says the capsules can be taken together or spread through the day. The vitamin blend lists niacin, pantothenic acid, biotin, vitamin B6, thiamin, riboflavin, folic acid (as calcium 5-methyltetrahydrofolate) and vitamin B12 (as cyanocobalamin), which the vendor's panel gives as 100% of the reference intake (RI). The vendor says the capsules are suitable for vegetarians and vegans.
howItWorks: Citicoline (500mg, as Cognizin®) is a precursor to acetylcholine and phosphatidylcholine; its memory evidence comes from older adults with inefficient memory at 1,000-2,000mg a day (Spiers 1996), and a Cochrane review found no evidence of an attention benefit in older adults with chronic cerebral disorders. Bacopa (300mg) has the most memory evidence here: two 12-week trials in healthy older adults improved delayed word recall at 300mg a day (Calabrese 2008; Morgan & Stevens 2010), though the newest 12-week trial at that dose (Lopresti 2025) found no effect on verbal learning, attention or working memory. Our reference dose is for an extract with at least 50% bacosides, and this label does not print the bacoside content. The positive ginkgo trials were in dementia, mainly at 240mg a day of the EGb 761 extract for 22-26 weeks (Tan 2015 meta-analysis); this product has 120mg with no standardisation on the product page, and the GEM trial found no preventive effect on dementia in people aged 75 and over. Rhodiola is an adaptogen: small trials of the SHR-5 extract found less mental fatigue, but a 2012 systematic review rated every included study at high or unclear risk of bias, and the product page does not say which extract or standardisation is used. We have no reference dose on file for Panax ginseng. Brain Capsules themselves have not been tested in a published trial; the vendor's claims rest on ingredient-level research.
whatToExpect: Brain Capsules are built for daily use rather than a quick effect: the vendor recommends taking them every day for at least 30 days to experience the full benefits, and the positive bacopa memory trials ran for 12 weeks. There is no caffeine, so the timing is flexible, and the vendor says they can be taken alongside its caffeinated drink. Take 3 capsules a day. Our bacopa page notes digestive effects (increased stool frequency, abdominal cramps, nausea) at 300mg a day in a 12-week trial in older adults, so taking the capsules with food may help. Its shipping help article (https://neutonic-support.gorgias.help/en-US/articles/shipping-delivery-434455, checked 2026-10-19) says 'If you're ordering from outside one of our local fulfilment regions, your order may be subject to import duties, taxes, VAT or customs processing fees.'
regulatoryNote: Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) publishes two ingredient lists that separate foods from medicines: Attachment 1, ingredients used exclusively as medicines (https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/001734637.pdf), and Attachment 2, ingredients not judged to be medicines unless a medicinal effect is claimed (https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/001734639.pdf), both updated 2026-08-05. Checked 2026-10-19: Ginkgo biloba, Bacopa monnieri, Rhodiola rosea and Panax ginseng each appear on Attachment 2 and none of them on Attachment 1; citicoline is named in neither list. No Foods with Function Claims (FFC) notification was found for Neutonic or Project Nootropic Ltd, the company behind neutonic.com, in the Consumer Affairs Agency (CAA) database (full export of 11,547 notifications scanned 2026-10-19).
